ELUCIDATION

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANA TORAJA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
GENERAL
Women and children are God's creatures who possess dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in the effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.

Fourth Part
Protection of Women

CHAPTER XIII
CRIMINAL SANCTIONS
Article 63
Every person or institution that commits acts resulting in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, coercion, or deprivation of liberty against women and children such that a violation of this regional regulation occurs, shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 30
Every child receives protection in the field of education as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter c, to obtain education.
The Regional Government, parents, and family must provide the widest possible opportunity to children to obtain education from an early age.
The Regional Government provides adequate facilities and infrastructure to support the teaching and learning process for children.
Non-governmental institutions may provide teaching and learning facilities and infrastructure for children, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 50
The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.
The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to: care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;
develop children in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests;
prevent the occurrence of marriage at child age; and provide character education and instillation of moral values in children.
Guardians and/or foster parents who have obtained a determination as referred to in Article 46 paragraph (3), must be able to fulfill the provisions as referred to in article 36 paragraph (2) letter a.
Guardians and/or foster parents who are appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have similarity with the religion adhered to by the Child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) are responsible for the child and must manage the property belonging to the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 52
P2TP2A as referred to in Article 51 paragraph (3) letter a, is positioned at the regional level and sub-district level.
P2TP2A is under the coordination of OPD or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.
P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate policies on women's empowerment and child protection.
P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit, which functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;
b. a service center for women and children victims of violence; and an empowerment center for women and children.

Article 26
Protection in the field of health as referred to in Article 25 paragraph (2) letter a, is carried out by the government through the provision of health facilities and efforts to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains the optimal degree of health from the time they are in the womb.
Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented by the Regional Government free of charge for families who are unable to afford them.

1.6.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 50 ayat (2) huruf c explicitly states parents must "mencegah terjadinya perkawinan pada usia anak" (prevent marriage at child age). Child/early marriage is commonly treated as a harmful practice. Since this is directly in the retrieved passage (Article 50) and the judge’s reasoning matches the Indonesian provision, the golden label of "No" appears incorrect.

2.1.evaluator_rationale: The passages describe coordination and networks within the Regional Government and with the community (e.g., sub-district/village units and integrated prevention), but none explicitly mention coordination or cooperation with governments across different jurisdictions (e.g., other regencies/provinces/national government).

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and children or mother and children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree.

Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custodial power as a parent over a child.

Every child who becomes a perpetrator or victim of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

Every operator of hotels, motels, inns, tourism guesthouse businesses and similar business activities is prohibited from renting rooms to children without being accompanied by parents or adult family members or supervising teachers/persons in charge in the context of carrying out school activities or other activities.

Second Part
Regional Government

CHAPTER XIII
CRIMINAL SANCTIONS
Article 63
Every person or institution that commits acts resulting in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, coercion, or deprivation of liberty against women and children such that a violation of this regional regulation occurs, shall be subject to criminal sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

2.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text defines PPT and P2TP2A as "jejaring kerjasama" (a cooperation network) (Pasal 1), and mandates prevention efforts be done "secara terpadu" with "koordinasi, integrasi, sinkronisasi" and forming "jaringan kerja" between government institutions and the community (Pasal 15 and Pasal 24). This is an explicit institutional coordination/network mechanism, and it is present in the retrieved candidates. The judge incorrectly required cross-jurisdiction (other regencies/provinces/national) coordination, which is not what the indicator necessarily requires. Given the document clearly establishes coordination mechanisms, the golden label "Yes" is supported; thus the discrepancy is best explained by evaluation failure.

2.3.evaluator_rationale: The passage explicitly includes “developing gender-based information systems,” which constitutes establishing an information/data system relevant to women’s protection and VAW-related programming.

GENERAL
Women and children are God's creatures who possess dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in the effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.

GENERAL
Women and children are God's creatures who possess dignity and human rights that need to be respected and valued.
Women are the pillars of the nation and children are the buds of the next generation of the nation's ideals and struggles. That children, who will later bear great responsibility as the next generation of the nation, need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially, so that children have noble character.
Women and children have a strategic role in determining the success of development programs in all aspects of state life. However, due to the still low understanding of the dignity of women and children, this makes them vulnerable to becoming victims of violence and discrimination both within the family and in their environment.
Various acts of violence against women and children continue to increase from time to time. If there is no awareness to provide serious attention and handling, it will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state.
Considering this, it is time that a regulation is needed in the form of a regional regulation on the Protection of Women and Children that is capable of responding while providing legal certainty for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence and discrimination.
As a concrete step in the effort to provide Protection of Women and Children in Tana Toraja Regency, through the initiative of the DPRD, a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children was drafted as an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 35 Year 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 8 Year 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities and Regulation of the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Number 6 Year 2015 concerning the System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of violence.
In this regional regulation, the rights of Women and Children, Women's Empowerment, Prevention, Protection of Women and Children are regulated. Also regulated are special handling of neglected children, responsibilities of the regional government, responsibilities of the Lembang government, up to Community, parental and Family Participation in the prevention, protection and handling of Women and Children.
This regional regulation also regulates financing sourced from APBD, APBL and other sources that are not binding, which is expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
